segments: The 17th cycle.
The Arab kings.
The Arabs, however, took captives as far as Chalcedon and remained.
And in the year 981 of the Greeks, Constantine commanded that to him and to his brothers,
Tiberius and Heraclius,
the Romans should submit equally,
and that on coins the effigies of all three of them should appear.
And he warned that no one should sow division among them.
And he went to Gaul and Italy,
and subdued all the western nations.
The Arabs, however, invaded {OCR?: ܩܠܥܘ/ܥܠܘ} Africa,
and took captive about eighty thousand people.
And after a year, they again took captives in Lycia and Cilicia.
And they returned again to Lycia,
and there came against them three patricians of the Romans,
and defeated them.
And there fell {OCR?: ܢܦܠܘ} of the Arabs about thirty thousand.
And those who remained took to the ships,
and were tossed about on the waves.
Now a certain carpenter, a native of Baalbek, whose name was Callinicus, prepared fire
and burned the ships of the Arabs.
And from here the Romans learned to prepare fire with naphtha.
Up to this time, only the Arabs were victorious,
but from this point on they were both victorious and defeated.
Constantine also sent certain Roman bandits, rebels, that is to say, outlaws,
who were called Mardaites by the Syrians.
And they seized from Mount Galilee up to the Black Mountain,
and the whole of Mount Lebanon,
and the Arabs suffered greatly from them.
And at last the Arabs grew strong,
and some of them they killed,
and the eyes of some of them they blinded.
Now Constantine, when a son was born {OCR?: ܐܫܬܘܫܛ / ܐܬܝܠܕ} to him, Justinian,
deposed his brothers from the kingdom,
and won over the leaders with gifts.
Now Leo, one of the magnates, who did not consent,
the king ordered that his tongue, his hands, and his feet should be cut off.
And when the executioner (the mob,
that is, the people? [a gloss]) was following him, and he was walking, he cried out:
"Neither do I deny the Trinity in heaven,
nor do I reject the trinity on earth."
And while crying out these things,
he received the stroke of the sentence.
And Constantine brought his brothers before the Roman grandees {patricians} and said to them:
"O Tiberius, and you, Heraclius,
what do you call me? Your brother,
or your king? If you call me king,
I will call you my brothers.
If, however, you call me brother,
I will consider you enemies."
